title: Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) Governance
summary: The governance of AEOs evolved from a basic recognition process to a sophisticated institutional framework involving specialized committees and centers. The Commissioner's role transitioned from a singular decision-maker to a key member of a centralized AEO Center and risk management committee structure.

evolution.institutions: Transitioned from a single committee to a centralized AEO Center and multi-agency risk management committees.
evolution.procedure: Increased formalization of application, audit, and appeal processes involving the Commissioner.

timeline.change: Defined AEO and established the initial AEO Committee chaired by the Commissioner.
Created the AEO Center and mandated the nomination of a Commissioner-rank officer as Director General.
Formalized the role of AEO special teams at customs stations under the Commissioner's coordination.
Integrated the Commissioner into the central Integrated Risk Management Committee (IRMC).

Authorized Economic Operator: An Authorized Economic Operator is defined as an entity that has received a recognition certificate from the Commissioner of Customs (Valuation and Internal Audit) under the relevant rules of this instrument.
Customs Act 1969: In this instrument, the term 'the Act' refers to the Customs Act 1969 (Act No. IV of 1969).
Application: An application is defined as a formal request submitted in the specified form as prescribed under the provisions of these rules.
Applicant: An applicant is defined as an economic operator engaged in customs-related activities who has submitted an application for the purpose of obtaining Authorized Economic Operator status.
Authorized Economic Operator (AEO) Commi: The committee is defined as the specific body established under the rules to oversee matters related to Authorized Economic Operators.
Commissioner of Customs Valuation and In: The Commissioner is defined as the officer holding the designation mentioned in the relevant section of the Customs Act 1969 regarding the Customs Valuation and Internal Audit Commissionerate.
Officer of Customs: A customs officer is defined according to the meaning provided in the relevant definition section of the Customs Act 1969.
Form: The term form refers to any of the specific formats or documents prescribed within these rules.
National Board of Revenue: The Board is defined as the National Board of Revenue established under the National Board of Revenue Order, 1972.
Recognition Certificate: A recognition certificate is defined as the document issued under the sub-rules of this instrument granting formal recognition to an Authorized Economic Operator.

Authorized Economic Operator: Commissioner of Customs (Valuation and Internal Audit)
Commissioner of Customs Valuation and In: Customs Valuation and Internal Audit Commissionerate

Authorized Economic Operator: A committee designated as the Authorized Economic Operator Committee is established to oversee and manage matters related to the Authorized Economic Operator program.

The committee is composed of several high-ranking customs officials, including a chairperson, the first secretary of the National Board of Revenue, and representatives from customs intelligence and investigation departments.
National Board of Revenue: The board is represented within the Authorized Economic Operator committee through the participation of its first secretary.
Customs Intelligence and Investigation D: The Director General of this directorate is responsible for nominating a senior official to serve as a member of the Authorized Economic Operator committee.
Customs Valuation and Internal Audit Com: This commissionerate provides necessary representation to the Authorized Economic Operator committee through officials nominated by the commissioner, including the member-secretary.

Authorized Economic Operator: first secretary of the National Board of Revenue
representatives from customs intelligence and investigation departments

National Board of Revenue: The Board is responsible for establishing the Authorized Economic Operator Center, including appointing a Director General from among its senior officers.
The Board is supported by the Center in coordinating mutual recognition agreements with other countries and in formulating policies and strategies regarding Authorized Economic Operators.
Authorized Economic Operator: The Center is formed by the Board to manage the recognition process, auditing, monitoring, and compliance of Authorized Economic Operators.
It acts as a liaison between customs offices and stakeholders to facilitate trade and ensure the effective implementation of authorized operations.
Until the formal establishment of the Center, its functions are to be discharged by the Customs Valuation and Internal Audit Commissionerate.

The Center manages the entire lifecycle of an Authorized Economic Operator, from processing initial applications and issuing temporary certificates to auditing, upgrading, downgrading, or revoking recognition status.
Authorized Economic Operators receive benefits related to customs procedure simplification and guaranteed service delivery as coordinated by the Center and local teams.
Every customs station must establish an Authorized Economic Operator team to ensure the smooth execution of related activities and provide proper services to recognized entities.
Each team is required to nominate a focal point officer to manage coordination with the central Authorized Economic Operator body.
Customs Valuation and Internal Audit Com: This office is designated to perform the functions of the Authorized Economic Operator Center until the Center is formally established.
During this interim period, its Commissioner and officers hold the authority and representative powers of the Center's Director General and corresponding staff.

Authorized Economic Operator: Customs Valuation and Internal Audit Commissionerate

member_objects.resolved_text: ৭. সভার নোটিশ প্রাপ্তির পর কাস্টমস গোয়েন্দা ও তদন্ত অধিদপ্তর (CIID), কাস্টমস রিস্ক ম্যানেজমেন্ট কমিশনারেট (CRMC), কাস্টমস মূল্যায়ন ও অভ্যন্তরীণ নিরীক্ষা কমিশনারেট (CVIAC), সেন্ট্রাল ইন্টেলিজেন্স সেল (CIC) এর প্রতিনিধিগণ স্ব স্ব দপ্তরে রক্ষিত গোয়েন্দা তথ্য-উপাত্ত, রেকর্ড, ঝুঁকি বিশ্লেষণ, প্রভৃতি পর্যালোচনা করে পরিশিষ্ট ২.১ মোতাবেক আবেদনকারী প্রতিষ্ঠানের বিষয়ে একটি প্রতিবেদন প্রস্তুত করে সংশ্লিষ্ট কমিশনার বা মহাপরিচালকের অনুস্বাক্ষর গ্রহণপূর্বক কমিটির সদস্য সচিব বরাবর প্রেরণ করবে।

Customs Intelligence and Investigation D: This entity must review internal intelligence reports, records, and risk analysis data upon receiving a meeting notice.
They are required to prepare a report based on their findings, obtain approval from their Director General, and submit it to the committee member secretary.
Customs Risk Management Commissionerate: This entity is responsible for evaluating intelligence data and risk management records following a meeting notification.
They must prepare and submit a formal report regarding the applicant institution to the committee member secretary after obtaining the relevant Commissioner's signature.
Customs Valuation and Internal Audit Com: This entity is tasked with reviewing relevant valuation and audit data upon notification of a meeting.
They are required to draft a report on the applicant and ensure it is signed by the Commissioner before forwarding it to the committee member secretary.
Central Intelligence Cell: This entity must analyze its held intelligence and data records upon receiving a notice for a committee meeting.
They are instructed to finalize a report on the applicant and submit it to the committee member secretary after obtaining the necessary institutional authorization.

member_objects.resolved_text: ১৮. কমিশনার স্বীকৃতিপ্রাপ্ত প্রতিষ্ঠানের জন্য প্রযোজ্য সুবিধাদি নিশ্চিতকরণ এবং AEO সেন্টারেরসহ অন্যান্য দপ্তরের সাথে যোগাযোগ ও সমন্বয়ের জন্য প্রত্যেকটি কাস্টমস স্টেশনে প্রয়োজনীয় সংখ্যক কাস্টমস কর্মকর্তার সমন্বয়ে AEO বিশেষ টিম গঠন করবে। উক্ত টিমকে স্বীকৃতিপ্রাপ্ত প্রতিষ্ঠানের জন্য সেবা প্রদান এবং প্রতিষ্ঠানের কোনো জিজ্ঞাসা থাকলে তার জবাব প্রদান প্রদান করবে। গঠিত AEO বিশেষ টিম স্বীকৃতিপ্রাপ্ত প্রতিষ্ঠানের জন্য প্রযোজ্য সুবিধাদি নিশ্চিতকরণ এবং AEO সেন্টারেরসহ অন্যান্য দপ্তরের সাথে যোগাযোগ ও সমন্বয় করবে।

Authorized Economic Operator: The customs station commissioner is required to form a dedicated special team to ensure that facilities and benefits are provided to accredited operators. This team acts as the primary point of contact for these operators, addressing their inquiries and facilitating communication with the AEO center and other relevant offices.
The special customs team established by the commissioner is responsible for coordinating and maintaining communication with the AEO center to support the needs of accredited operators.
Commissioner of Customs: The commissioner is mandated to establish a special customs team at every customs station to ensure that benefits for accredited operators are delivered and that efficient coordination with relevant departments is maintained.

Integrated Risk Management Committee: The National Board of Revenue is mandated to form a centralized Integrated Risk Management Committee to fulfill the objectives of the Customs Risk Management Rules 2025.

The committee is composed of various senior customs officials, including members of the customs wing, commissioners of customs stations, bond commissioners, the head of customs intelligence, and specific representatives from the risk management directorate.
The committee holds quarterly meetings to review customs risk management protocols.
National Board of Revenue: The Board acts as the authorizing body responsible for the establishment and composition of the Integrated Risk Management Committee.
Customs Risk Management Commissionerate: The Commissioner of this directorate serves as a core member of the Integrated Risk Management Committee, and its Additional or Joint Commissioner serves as the member secretary.

Integrated Risk Management Committee: representatives from the risk management directorate

Authorized Economic Operator: This form is the prescribed application document used for obtaining certification as an Authorized Economic Operator.
Applicants must adhere to the formal requirements set out in the Authorised Economic Operator (Certification) Rules 2018 when submitting their application to the Commissioner.
Self-Assessment Questionnaire: The application for Authorized Economic Operator status requires the submission of a completed Self-Assessment Questionnaire.
Applicants are required to attach all necessary supporting documentation along with the completed questionnaire to validate their application.
Commissioner of Customs: The application for Authorized Economic Operator status is formally addressed to the Commissioner of the relevant Customs Assessment and Internal Audit Commissionerate.
